summary: A spread-out craft outing east of Chiang Mai: watch umbrella making in Bo Sang, choose a few silk, lacquerware or celadon workshops along Highway 1006, and optionally add MAIIAM contemporary art museum. It works best as a deliberately selected route rather than an attempt to visit every storefront.
whyGo: See Bo Sang artisans make and paint bamboo-and-saa-paper umbrellas, with a craft shop nearby.
Browse several northern Thai craft traditions along the San Kamphaeng road, including silk, lacquerware and celadon ceramics.
Pair living craft traditions with Thai and regional contemporary art at MAIIAM, in the same district.
bestFor: Travelers interested in making processes and locally produced crafts.
A flexible half-day or full-day outing by private car or hired driver.
Visitors who want a museum or shopping stop outside the Old City.
skipIf: You need a compact, easily walkable attraction: stops are scattered along a busy road.
You expect every workshop to be operating or offering demonstrations; activity and visitor arrangements vary by business.
duration: Allow 3–5 hours for Bo Sang plus two or three selected craft stops; a full day if adding MAIIAM and a farther-eastern stop. These are planning estimates because the corridor has no single visitor route or standard visit length. Bo Sang alone is commonly a 1–2 hour visit.
cost: Bo Sang village and umbrella-making viewing are listed as free; purchases and any hands-on activity cost extra, with workshop prices varying. MAIIAM currently lists adult admission at 200 THB (students 100 THB, seniors 150 THB). Budget for transport between stops; recheck museum and workshop prices before December 2026.
hours: Bo Sang’s official tourism listing gives daily hours of 08:00–17:00; a Chiang Mai provincial publication gives 08:30–17:00. Individual craft shops set their own hours. MAIIAM’s visit page has conflicting schedules: one section says every day except Tuesday, 10:00–18:00, while the footer says Friday–Monday, 10:00–18:00. Confirm directly before planning around it.
bestTime: Start in the morning, when workshops are more likely to be active and there is time to continue east. December is outside Bo Sang’s usual Umbrella and San Kamphaeng Handicrafts Festival period, which falls in January; no December 2026 corridor event was verified.
gettingThere: Bo Sang is roughly 9–13 km east of central Chiang Mai, on or near Highway 1006 (San Kamphaeng Road). A car, Grab or chartered red songthaew offers the most control between dispersed stops. MAIIAM’s official page describes a white public minibus from Warorot Market to San Kamphaeng, currently 15 THB, with citybound service until about 18:00; confirm route and service on the day. The road can be congested.
booking: No advance booking information is published for Bo Sang viewing; ask individual studios before visiting if a specific demonstration or hands-on session matters. MAIIAM’s official visit page gives visitor information but no booking requirement; check its current opening schedule and exhibitions before setting out.
accessibility: No reliable access information was found for the corridor as a whole. It consists of separate roadside shops and workshops, so surfaces, steps, toilets and vehicle drop-off will differ by stop. Contact chosen venues about step-free entry and accessible facilities. MAIIAM lists parking, but its visit page does not detail step-free access.
practicalTips: Pick two or three named stops in advance and arrange transport between them; the busy highway and spread-out workshops make an improvised walking route impractical.
At Bo Sang, ask before photographing artisans or entering work areas; buy directly from the maker if you want a finished piece.
If visiting MAIIAM, check the official schedule because its current page gives conflicting weekly opening days.
Carry cash for small purchases and confirm whether a chosen workshop accepts cards; payment methods vary and were not consistently published.
decemberNotes: December is a useful time for an outdoor craft route, but workshop activity is business-specific and no special December 2026 event was confirmed. The Bo Sang umbrella festival is generally held in January, so do not plan on festival displays or a parade in December. Confirm individual hours shortly before travel and especially confirm MAIIAM’s opening days.
uncertainties: MAIIAM’s own visit page conflicts about weekly opening days; verify directly for the intended December date.
No unified corridor schedule, current workshop price list or dependable accessibility listing exists in the sources reviewed.
